log.text: Light Screen up on P2's side

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega Gengar. Lead Gengar+Sneasler: Fake Out Whim/Grim to deny Tailwind/screens, Sludge Bomb 4x Whim and 2x Grim for KO. Sneasler Rock Slide 4x Zard punishes Protect read. Back Staraptor Intimidate+BraveBird+Tailwind and Dragonite Multiscale EQ covers Archaludon/Stunfisk and speed control.
decisions.notebook: Opp sun HO: ZardY Timid HW/WeatherBall/Hurricane/Protect, Whim Bold Prankster Tailwind/Encore/Moonblast/Protect Leftovers, Grim Impish Light Clay screens FakeOut/PartingShot, Arch Modest Stamina WiseGlasses TBolt/Flash/Draco/Protect, Stunfisk-G Impish SoftSand EQ/IceFang/TWave/Protect, Quaq Jolly MysticWater AquaStep/CC/IceSpinner/Protect. Game1 bring Zard/Whim/Grim/Arch. Tends Zard Protect T1 vs Rock Slide, Arch Protect stalls CC drops. Game2 may bring Stunfisk/Quaq. Keep FakeOut+RockSlide pressure and Intimidate+Tailwind.

decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott + Grimmsnarl for double Prankster priority. Both resist Fighting spam from Staraptor/Sneasler. Turn 1: Fake Out one threat, Tailwind or Encore the other, then Parting Shot into Quaquaval or Stunfisk-Galar who resist Rock Slide and threaten back. Save Charizard-Mega-Y for mid-game after Fighting threats are eliminated to avoid Rock Slide KO.
decisions.notebook: Opponent relies on double Fighting spam (Staraptor/Sneasler) with Rock Slide coverage. Kingambit and Dragonite provide priority cleanup. Gengar-Mega is Shadow Tag trapper. My counter: Whimsicott/Grimmsnarl double Prankster lead resists Fighting, pivots with Parting Shot into Quaquaval/Stunfisk who handle Rock Slide. Charizard-Mega-Y is mid-game win condition after Fighting threats removed. Game 1 win suggests opponent expects aggressive leads; double Prankster disrupts their tempo.

decisions.rationale: Sludge Bomb is 160-510% guaranteed OHKO vs Whim, Sneasler 189 > Whim 168 so we outspeed. Fake Out Grim (Dark immune to Prankster Encore) prevents Reflect/LightScreen. Mega gives Shadow Tag to block PartingShot pivot. Protect on Whim only stalls one turn.
decisions.notebook: Opp sun HO: ZardY Timid HW/WeatherBall/Hurricane/Protect, Whim Bold Prankster Tailwind/Encore/Moonblast/Protect Leftovers, Grim Impish Light Clay screens FakeOut/PartingShot, Arch Modest Stamina WiseGlasses TBolt/Flash/Draco/Protect, Stunfisk-G Impish SoftSand EQ/IceFang/TWave/Protect, Quaq Jolly MysticWater AquaStep/CC/IceSpinner/Protect. Game1 bring Zard/Whim/Grim/Arch. Tends Zard Protect T1 vs Rock Slide, Arch Protect stalls CC drops. Keep FakeOut+RockSlide pressure and Intimidate+Tailwind.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Whimsicott)
decisions.rationale: Gengar will Mega Evolve into Shadow Tag, trapping us. Sneasler's Fake Out outspeeds Prankster. Protect keeps Whimsicott safe from 4x Poison Jab/Sludge Bomb while Grimmsnarl sets Light Screen to mitigate Gengar-Mega's special damage. Screens let us survive turn 1 and reassess turn 2 without losing a Prankster user.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Gengar (Gengarite) + Sneasler (Focus Sash). Gengar-Mega = Shadow Tag trapper, blocks all switches. Sneasler Fake Out priority +3 outspeeds Prankster. Double Prankster lead resists Fighting but cannot switch once Shadow Tag is active. Turn 1 plan: Protect Whimsicott, Light Screen with Grimmsnarl to survive Gengar-Mega special attacks. Post-screen plan: Moonblast Sneasler to break Focus Sash, then KO next turn; use Encore if Gengar-Mega uses Protect. Quaquaval/Stunfisk cannot be brought in until Gengar-Mega is KOed. Charizard-Mega-Y win condition delayed until Shadow Tag removed. Opponent likely double Fighting spam core; Kingambit/Dragonite back for priority cleanup.

decisions.rationale: Gengar Sludge Bomb OHKOs Whim even through Light Screen (215% min -> 107% halved). Sneasler Poison Jab also OHKOs Whim. Targeting Whim with Gengar guarantees Tailwind denial even if Whim Prankster Encores Sneasler before it moves. Sneasler into Grimmsnarl gives best chance to remove screens setter (Grim at 89% HP, Gengar min 89.1% max).

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Whimsicott)
decisions.rationale: Prankster Encore (+1 priority) outspeeds Gengar-Mega, locking it into Sludge Bomb for 3 turns. Grimmsnarl's Prankster Light Screen also moves first, setting special defense before opponents attack. This gives predictability against the trapper and survivability to break Sneasler's Focus Sash next turn with Moonblast, then pivot to Quaquaval/Stunfisk once Gengar-Mega falls.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag blocks all switches until it's KOed. Double Prankster lead provides +1 priority status. Turn 1 Light Screen failed (Grimmsnarl flinched by Sneasler Fake Out). Sneasler holds Focus Sash + Unburden. Plan: Encore Gengar-Mega into Sludge Bomb, set Light Screen, Moonblast Sneasler to break sash, KO Gengar-Mega to enable Quaquaval/Stunfisk pivot. Opponent back: Dragonite (Multiscale/Lum, Tailwind/ExtSpeed/Earthquake/Protect), Kingambit (Supreme Overlord/LO, Kowtow/IronHead/SuckerPunch/Protect), Sinistcha (Heatproof/Leftovers, MatchaGotcha/RagePowder/ShadowBall/Protect), Staraptor (Intimidate/SharpBeak, BraveBird/CloseCombat/Tailwind/Protect). Charizard-Mega-Y win condition delayed until Shadow Tag removed.

decisions.rationale: Stunfisk-Galar is immune to Gengar's Encored Sludge Bomb and resists Sneasler's Close Combat and Rock Slide. It enters for free, threatening both foes with Earthquake or Thunder Wave, allowing us to break Sneasler's sash or pressure Gengar while Light Screen is up.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag blocks switches until KOed. Sneasler holds Focus Sash + Unburden. Opponent back: Dragonite (Multiscale/Lum), Kingambit (Supreme Overlord/LO), Sinistcha (Heatproof/Leftovers), Staraptor (Intimidate/SharpBeak). Plan: Stunfisk-Galar walls Encored Sludge Bomb and resists Sneasler's physical moves. Use Earthquake/Thunder Wave to pressure the field. Break Sneasler's sash or KO Gengar to free up switches for Quaquaval.

decisions.rationale: Gengar Encored to Sludge Bomb immune vs Stunfisk so must hit Grimmsnarl 11% to deny PartingShot. Sneasler before Grimmsnarl so CC hits Stunfisk before debuff, 69-152% range chance OHKO. Shadow Tag keeps trap, even if EQ 52-135% KOs Gengar we trade 1 for 1+ damage and keep sash Sneasler.
decisions.notebook: Opp sun HO: ZardY Timid HW/WeatherBall/Hurricane/Protect, Whim Bold Leftovers Tailwind/Encore/Moonblast/Protect, Grim Impish LightClay screens FakeOut/PartingShot, Arch Modest WiseGlasses TBolt/Flash/Draco/Protect, Stunfisk-G Impish SoftSand EQ/IceFang/TWave/Protect, Quaq Jolly MysticWater AquaStep/CC/IceSpinner/Protect. Game1 bring Zard/Whim/Grim/Arch. Tends Zard Protect T1 vs Rock Slide, Arch Protect stalls CC drops. Keep FakeOut+RockSlide pressure and Intimidate+Tailwind. ShadowTag blocks PartingShot switch.

decisions.rationale: Grimmsnarl lacks Protect and will be KOed by Encored Sludge Bomb. Parting Shot on Gengar lowers its SpA and safely pivots to Quaquaval, who takes a neutral, now-weakened Sludge Bomb. Stunfisk Earthquake spreads 2x damage to break Sneasler's sash or KO Gengar.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag blocks switches until KOed. Sneasler Focus Sash + Unburden confirmed. Gengar Encored Sludge Bomb. Opponent back: Dragonite (Multiscale/Lum), Kingambit (Supreme Overlord/LO), Sinistcha (Heatproof/Leftovers), Staraptor (Intimidate/SharpBeak). Plan: Break Sneasler sash or KO Gengar to free switches for Quaquaval. Grimmsnarl Parting Shot pivot available to bring in Quaquaval safely. Stunfisk walls Sludge Bomb (immune) and resists Sneasler physicals.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Sneasler 378 Unburden outspeeds and CC KOs Stunfisk 29% (69-152% max) before EQ, removing spread threat. Gengar locked to Sludge Bomb immune vs Stunfisk and -1 SpA through Light Screen unlikely to KO Quaquaval, so switch to Staraptor for EQ immunity and Intimidate to blunt Quaquaval, preserving Gengar 20% in back and leaving full HP Staraptor vs low Quaquaval.

Sneasler outspeeds everything and will Close Combat. Quaquaval Protect dodges the KO; Stunfisk Thunder Wave punishes the likely double-target on Quaquaval by paralyzing Sneasler, keeping both my mons alive and crippling their speedster. Fallback if they read Protect: lose Stunfisk but Quaquaval survives to clean 1% Sneasler and pressure 19% Gengar next turn.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Staraptor BB OHKO Quaq (101-299%) and Sneasler CC kills Quaq from 27% even at -1 Intimidate, so double targeting Quaq guarantees its removal despite one FakeOut (+3 priority). Grim at 11% left is low threat and cleaned next turn by any attack. Protecting or splitting risks leaving Quaq alive to IceSpinner Staraptor.

Sneasler cannot Fake Out (used turn 1). Grimmsnarl Fake Out Staraptor (priority +3) flinches the 100% threat before it moves. Quaquaval Ice Spinner Staraptor (2x SE, 41-127%) aims to KO and remove Intimidate/Brave Bird pressure. Worst case Sneasler Rock Slides or Poison Jabs Grimmsnarl (12%), but Quaquaval survives and Staraptor is flinched or KOed.
decisions.notebook: Sneasler Fake Out is one-time per switch-in (turn 1 use). Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag blocks switches when active. Opponent back: Dragonite (Multiscale/Lum), Kingambit (SupremeOverlord/LO), Sinistcha (Heatproof/Leftovers). Plan: KO Staraptor to remove Intimidate/Brave Bird, then pivot Quaquaval into Gengar-Mega with Ice Spinner or Close Combat. Grimmsnarl is sacrificial pivot at 12% HP. Quaquaval Atk -1 from Intimidate turn 4. Light Screen active 5 turns.

decisions.rationale: Grim at 11% must die before Reflect/Parting Shot. Staraptor outspeeds and Brave Bird KOs. Sneasler at 1% -3 gets value with Rock Slide hitting incoming slot; 4x vs Zard-Y is best punish, also hits Grim. Light Screen reduces special damage so Staraptor survives spread.

I have no Pokémon left to switch in, forcing a pass on Quaquaval's slot. Grimmsnarl should use Reflect to mitigate physical damage from Staraptor's Brave Bird and Sneasler's attacks, extending its survivability. Parting Shot would force a switch and cause an immediate loss since I have no backups.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Gengar-Mega + Sneasler. Sneasler Fake Outs turn 1 then uses Close Combat. Gengar-Mega spams Sludge Bomb. Staraptor switches in to Intimidate. Opponent back: Dragonite, Kingambit, Sinistcha.

reflections.summary: Won because preview was perfect for their Game2 non-sun bring (Whim/Grim/Quaq/Stunfisk). Mega Gengar Shadow Tag negated Grim Parting Shot pivot and Sludge Bomb OHKOed Whim + chunked Grim/Quaq, while Sneasler Poison Jab/CC/Rock Slide had super-effective coverage into all 4 and Focus Sash survived Stunfisk EQ at 1% to sweep. Staraptor Intimidate on switch-in neutered Quaq/Stunfisk physical pressure.
reflections.adjustment: Keep Mega Gengar to trap Grim and block Parting Shot, keep Sneasler sash intact for Stunfisk/Quaq. Lead Fake Out + Sludge Bomb to deny Whim Encore/Tailwind and break Grim screens early. Preserve Staraptor Intimidate vs EQ/Quaq instead of committing Dragonite Tailwind vs screens team.
reflections.notebook: Opp sun HO 6 confirmed. Game1 bring ZardY/Whim/Grim/Arch, Game2 bring Whim/Grim/Quaq/Stunfisk-G - pivots to screens + Fighting-weak offense when Zard denied. Tendencies: Whim Encore T1 vs Gengar, Grim Light Screen first then Reflect, Parting Shot into Gengar fails vs ShadowTag, Grim Fake Out late, Quaq Protects at low HP after Intimidate, Stunfisk EQ hits own ally Quaq. Light Clay screens (8T Reflect/4T Light Screen). Plan: Mega Gengar traps, Sludge Bomb/Poison Jab for Whim/Grim, Sneasler CC for Stunfisk/Quaq, Staraptor Intimidate + FakeOut/RockSlide pressure.

reflections.summary: The team preview was fundamentally mismatched against the opponent's hyper-offensive lead. Whimsicott and Grimmsnarl were too frail and slow to handle Gengar-Mega and Sneasler, resulting in rapid cascading faints. Whimsicott was KO'd on Turn 2 despite landing Encore, and Stunfisk-Galar was KO'd by Close Combat after failing to apply enough pressure. The team lacked a fast or bulky answer to the opponent's offensive core.
reflections.adjustment: Bring a bulky Dark-type or a faster attacker instead of Whimsicott or Stunfisk-Galar to handle Gengar-Mega and Sneasler. A Pokemon that can survive a hit and retaliate, or outspeed the opponent's core, is essential to avoid being overwhelmed by their offensive pressure.
reflections.notebook: Opponent leads Gengar-Mega (Timid) + Sneasler (Jolly, Focus Sash, Unburden). Sneasler Fake Outs turn 1 then spams Close Combat; Focus Sash breaks to activate Unburden. Gengar-Mega spams Sludge Bomb. Staraptor (Intimidate) switches in to Intimidate. Opponent back: Dragonite (Multiscale, Lum Berry, Tailwind), Kingambit (Supreme Overlord, Life Orb, Sucker Punch), Sinistcha (Heatproof, Rage Powder). Opponent strategy: hyper-offensive lead with Sneasler's Unburden speed and Gengar-Mega's power. Future plan: bring a bulky Dark-type or faster attacker to handle this lead; avoid frail support Pokemon.
